headline: Canadian wildfire hazard paper reports a fast AI surrogate for BurnP3+ mapping
summary: A 16 October arXiv v1 paper from Mila and Natural Resources Canada authors describes a multi-task U-Net surrogate for BurnP3+ wildfire-hazard mapping. Using simulator-derived outputs for burn probability, fire intensity and rate of spread, the authors report results across five held-out regions from a 54-region split and a three-seed model evaluation. On representative Region 16, they report 806.5× end-to-end CPU acceleration: 173.6 seconds on four CPU cores versus 38.9 hours for BurnP3+ on 32 cores, with 13% of the simulator's peak host memory. The authors report 0.85 intersection-over-union for high-hazard classes, but zero for the most extreme class 13. These are paper-reported comparisons against the simulator, not validation against observed fires or field decision outcomes; the underlying dataset is access-restricted and no independent reproduction was conducted. The arXiv cs.AI listing includes the paper on 23 October although the HTML v1 header says 16 October.
